narratives.title: Geopolitical Escalation Risk-Off
narratives.summary: Capital is fleeing risk assets as multi-front conflicts (US-Iran, Israel-Hezbollah, Ukraine-Russia) escalate beyond controlled tit-for-tat, with Iran shooting down a US Apache and threatening regional war expansion. The market consensus underestimates the persistence and structural nature of these disruptions, driving flows into safe havens.
narratives.trade_implication: Long VIX futures, short S&P 500 (SPY) and long gold (GLD) as hedges against continued escalation; reduce exposure to emerging market equities.

narratives.title: Oil Supply Disruption and Blockade
narratives.summary: Capital is rotating into energy assets as the Strait of Hormuz blockade persists through Q3 2026 per EIA, with Kuwait seeking bypass pipelines and US SPR release signaling structural tightness rather than bearish supply. The market misreads SPR as bearish, but actual flows show bullish positioning on oil due to prolonged disruption risk.
narratives.trade_implication: Long WTI crude futures (CL) and energy sector ETFs (XLE); consider long-dated call options on oil producers as blockade extends.

narratives.title: Diplomatic Off-Ramp Uncertainty
narratives.summary: Capital is hedging against binary outcomes as White House claims 'progress' on Iran deal while military actions (IDF readiness, Kuwait bypass talks) suggest no near-term resolution. The contradiction between diplomatic signals and kinetic reality keeps flows indecisive, with money moving into short-term Treasuries and cash.
narratives.trade_implication: Short-term US Treasuries (SHY) and USD (DXY) long; avoid long-duration bonds and currencies exposed to Middle East risk (e.g., Turkish lira).
